name: vision_ocr_ctc_bad
title: The same CRNN/CTC recogniser with eight planted defects
origin: domain-vision round 2: the dirty twin of vision_ocr_ctc; a user-defined Dataset subclass is what hides the augmented validation pipeline, and one int() in an unrelated binding is what hides the live-tensor accumulation

expected.why: every BatchNorm2d in the CRNN backbone updates its running statistics from the validation split and the dropout before the LSTM stays on, so the reported character error rate is measured on a model the training run then inherits

expected.defect: the training loader does not shuffle
expected.why: the crops are indexed in page order, so every batch is one document in one font and the recogniser overfits to it before the next page is reached

expected.symbol: for images, targets, target_lengths, widths, texts in loader
expected.why: the autograd graph for the whole validation split is built and discarded, which on long text lines is the difference between fitting in memory and not
the update has already been applied, so the clip only rescales gradients that are about to be zeroed - the exploding-gradient protection a recurrent head needs is not there

expected.defect: the validation split is read through the augmenting pipeline (ColorJitter)
expected.why: the character error rate is measured on jittered crops, so the validation curve moves for reasons that have nothing to do with the model
expected.gap: MLV114 requires the dataset construction to resolve to a knowledge-table DATASET row, so a user-defined torch.utils.data.Dataset subclass - the only way an OCR project can load `<id>_<text>.png` crops - is skipped in silence. Minimal repro in the round-2 report (VIS2-01).

expected.defect: the running loss keeps the live CTC loss tensor
expected.why: every batch's autograd graph is retained for the whole epoch, which on a bidirectional LSTM over 320-frame sequences is the memory the run dies on
expected.gap: the PUB-08 detach walk is a syntactic ast.walk over every transitively reaching binding, so the `int(w)` inside the `input_lengths` list comprehension at line 76 is read as proof that `running_loss` is a Python number. Minimal repro in the round-2 report (VIS2-02).

expected.defect: OneCycleLR is stepped once per epoch instead of once per batch
expected.why: the one-cycle schedule completes its whole cycle in the first three epochs and the remaining twenty-seven train at the floor learning rate - nothing raises, so the loss curve is the only evidence
expected.gap: MLV207's batch-cadence branch requires the epoch loop to lexically enclose the batch loop, and the batch loop lives in train_one_epoch(). Minimal repro in the round-2 report (VIS2-03).

expected.why: the sample predictions printed after each epoch are a different set of lines every time, so two runs cannot be compared line by line

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled rather than its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading the day model.py is renamed

expected.defect: nn.CTCLoss is fed F.softmax output where it requires log-probabilities
expected.why: CTC applies no normalisation of its own; plain probabilities make the loss finite, wrong and minimised by predicting blank everywhere, so the model converges to an empty transcription
expected.gap: no rule models the CTC input contract. MLV401 is the nearest analogue - it is the same class of defect, an activation contradicting the loss's own normalisation - but it is written for CrossEntropyLoss only.

forbidden.why: there is no sklearn transformer and no split in this project
same - nothing is fitted on anything here
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is still the first statement of the training step
optimizer.step() is still called every batch
loss.backward() still precedes optimizer.step(); only the clip moved
no backward() call is inside a no_grad region - validate() lost its decorator but contains no backward()
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in this project
the model is moved with .to(device) and every batch tensor is moved inside the loop
seed_everything() still seeds random, numpy, torch and torch.cuda
there is no sklearn split and no random_split in this project
ConvBlock, BidirectionalLSTM and CRNN all call super().__init__()
the convolutional stack is wrapped in nn.ModuleList
the only metric is a hand-written character error rate over decoded strings; no sklearn or torchmetrics class metric is called
no ranking metric is computed anywhere
there is no Keras model in this project
there is no Keras layer and no from_logits= anywhere

gaps.what: the CTC input lengths are computed from the padded width rather than the true width, so every sample is told it has more frames than it does and the alignment is free to put characters into the padding
gaps.evidence: dataset.py ctc_collate returns the true widths, and train.py:76 passes them - but the defective twin's model.downsampled_width() is applied to the padded tensor in neither version, so this is the shape the rule set would have to model, not a planted defect

gaps.what: no rule pairs nn.CTCLoss with the normalisation of its input, which is the direct analogue of MLV401 for sequence recognition
gaps.evidence: train.py:74 F.softmax against the clean twin's F.log_softmax; labelled above as MLV401/unsupported
